MONEO ERP exposes the Ping method of its _slave JSON-RPC service over WebSocket as @rpc.openpublic, so it can be called without a valid session. The method's only guard compares the calling application name with "_login", but that value is taken from the client-controlled params.appname field of the request. When the check passes, Ping stores an attacker-chosen session ID, user number and company in the server session store, and subsequent session validation accepts that session. An unauthenticated remote attacker can therefore create a valid session as any user, including administrators, in any company (tenant) hosted on the server and invoke authenticated RPC methods with that user's privileges, gaining read and write access to that company's data.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler. The vulnerability exists because the `remove_optimizations()` function reads attacker-controlled values from the unprotected `w3tc_imageservice` post meta key — which carries no underscore prefix and no registered authorization callback, making it writable by any user with `edit_post` capability via WordPress's built-in custom-fields AJAX endpoint — and passes those values directly to `wp_delete_attachment()` with no check that the referenced ID is a child of the caller's own post, is an actual attachment, or that the caller holds `delete_post` capability on it. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Author-level access or above to permanently delete any WordPress attachment in the media library, including media files owned by other users along with their associated files on disk, regardless of ownership — a capability not available through the normal WordPress interface. The revert nonce is exposed via `wp_localize_script` on `/wp-admin/upload.php` to any user with `upload_files` capability, ensuring the nonce check that is present does not serve as a meaningful barrier to Author-level exploitation.

A low-privileged network attacker or user who can search the directory sends a Virtual List View search by value, sorted on an attribute the matching entries do not have. The LDAP worker that handles the search exits, which disconnects the directory clients that were using that worker, and the directory service starts a replacement worker. Another search of the same kind crashes the worker that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that worker is replaced, so repeating the search keeps the LDAP service from staying available. The same crash follows a search sorted on an attribute the attacker is not allowed to read. The directory removes that attribute from the result, and the comparison uses the missing value.

The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the `SwpmLevelForm::role()` function applying only `sanitize_text_field()` to the user-supplied `role` parameter with no allowlist, permitting the `administrator` role to be stored verbatim into `swpm_membership_tbl` and subsequently applied to a member's WordPress account via `$user->add_role()` inside `update_wp_user_role()` — also without any role allowlist — when the `swpm_membership_level_changed` action fires. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to create a membership level specifying the `administrator` WordPress role, assign themselves to that level, and thereby elevate their own WordPress account to full Administrator, gaining complete site control including the ability to install plugins, edit themes, and manage users. Exploitation requires that the site owner has lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default `manage_options` capability to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts`, `edit_published_posts`, or `edit_pages`, which grants lower-privileged users access to the SWPM admin dashboard where the vulnerable level-creation form resides. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 The vulnerability exists because the `bulk_operation_menu()` function accepts the `swpm_bulk_change_level_to` parameter from `$_REQUEST` with only `sanitize_text_field()` applied, and passes it to `SwpmMemberUtils::update_membership_level_and_role()` without the `id != 1` allowlist exclusion that every other level-selection path in the plugin enforces — leaving membership level 1, which the installer maps to the WordPress `administrator` role on every fresh install, freely selectable as a bulk-change target. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to elevate their own WordPress account to the full Administrator role, gaining complete site control including plugin installation, user creation, and all other administrator capabilities. Exploitation requires that an administrator has first lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default of `manage_options` to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts` (Contributor), `edit_published_posts` (Author), or `edit_pages` (Editor), which is a non-default granted-access configuration; the bulk screen's nonce protection (`swpm_bulk_change_level_nonce_action`) does not mitigate the issue because the nonce is emitted on the same page the delegated lower-role user can already reach. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

The connector then reads secrets of other participants or of the runtime, such as STS client secrets or the encryption key, and sends them to an endpoint the attacker chooses.

A flaw has been found in Free5GC 4.3.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the component SMF. This manipulation causes resource consumption. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the eventbus execution in Google Cloud Application Integration versions prior to 2026-09-22 on Google Cloud Platform allows an authenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution using a crafted serialized Java object.


This vulnerability was patched on 22 September 2026, and no customer action is needed.

A vulnerability was identified in eosphoros-ai DB-GPT up to 0.8.3. The impacted element is the function get_editor_tables of the file packages/dbgpt-app/src/dbgpt_app/openapi/api_v1/editor/api_editor_v1.py of the component Editor API. Such manipulation of the argument db_name leads to improper access controls. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in David Lingren Media LIbrary Assistant media-library-assistant allows Blind SQL Injection.This issue affects Media LIbrary Assistant: from n/a through 3.43.

A Missing Authorization vulnerability in the private console API in Google Cloud Vertex AI (Vertex AI Assistant) versions prior to 2026-04-13 on Google Cloud Platform allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to list, read, create, and send messages in other users' chat sessions using crafted API requests.


This vulnerability was patched on 13 April 2026, and no customer action is needed.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in Hello Clever Pty Hello Clever Gateway for WooCommerce cleverpay-gateway allows SQL Injection.This issue affects Hello Clever Gateway for WooCommerce: from n/a through 1.8.4.

DoS vulnerability in BS2500/BS500 Virtage Firmware.

This issue affects BladeSymphony BS2500: from 02-02 through 02-76; BladeSymphony BS500: from 01-01 through 02-76.

A path traversal vulnerability in Medusa’s product import functionality, specifically in the handling of the 'file_key' parameter of the '/admin/products/imports' endpoint. The lack of proper validation allows an authenticated remote attacker with administrative access to reference system files outside the intended import directory. When attempting to process these files as CSV files, the application may partially reveal their contents through parsing or validation error messages. Additionally, cleanup routines operate on paths controlled by the attacker, which could allow the deletion of files accessible to the application process and affect system availability.

cves.description: The Smaily Connect plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 3.24.0 This is due to the smaily_get_edit_user_id() function reading an attacker-controlled $_GET['user_id'] parameter without performing any ownership or capability check, and then feeding that id into smaily_get_userdata() (which calls get_user_meta()) when rendering the WooCommerce My Account 'edit-account' form via the smaily_print_user_frontend_fields() handler on the woocommerce_edit_account_form action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to read other users' personally identifiable profile data (phone number, date of birth, and gender — including administrators') by appending ?user_id=<target> to the account-details URL.
Authentication Bypass by Spoofing vulnerability in TMS Amelia ameliabooking allows Identity Spoofing.This issue affects Amelia: from n/a through 2.4.14.

The Upsell Funnel Builder for WooCommerce – Create Upsells, Cross-Sells, Order Bumps, Frequently Bought, and Popups. plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce gating the vulnerable AJAX endpoint is publicly emitted to any visitor loading a cart, checkout, or shortcode page, making the endpoint fully exploitable by unauthenticated attackers without any prior account or login.
cves.product: Upsell Funnel Builder for WooCommerce – Create Upsells, Cross-Sells, Order Bumps, Frequently Bought, and Popups.

cves.description: The E2Pdf – Export Pdf Tool for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'your-name (or any CF7 field referenced in the action's error_message/condition)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.00.05 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a typical deployment where an E2Pdf action with a 'PDF Access By URL' error message references a submitted Contact Form 7 field, as the payload is seeded via a single unauthenticated CF7 submission and triggered by any visitor who opens the resulting shareable download URL.
cves.product: E2Pdf – Export Pdf Tool for WordPress

cves.description: Webmin through 2.670 before ae8feb1 allows XSS via an SVG attachment in a mail queue, relevant if an authenticated user uploads an SVG document and an administrator views it.

An Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs in the namespace onboarding API in Google Cloud GKE Fleet versions prior to 2026-09-25 on Google Cloud Platform allows an authenticated attacker to escalate privileges to project owner using a privileged system namespace onboarding request.


This vulnerability was patched on 25 September 2026, and no customer action is needed.

A weakness has been identified in TRENDnet TEW-751DR 1.03B01. This impacts the function FUN_0040ed90 of the file wfadev.cgi of the component UPnP/WFA. This manipulation of the argument SOAPAction causes stack-based buffer overflow. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. A high degree of complexity is needed for the attack. The exploitability is said to be difficult. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Script injection.

A security vulnerability has been detected in code-projects Online Job Portal 1.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file Admin/InsertUser.php. Such manipulation of the argument txtUserName/txtPassword leads to sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.
Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in weDevs WP ERP erp allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects WP ERP: from n/a through 2.0.0.

Kestra before 1.3.36 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute JavaScript by injecting HTML into the executions page sort parameter. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a crafted link whose invalid sort value is rendered unsanitized in an error toast, stealing the non-HttpOnly BASIC_AUTH credential cookie to take over the instance.

A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. When a system-wide app, runtime, or extension uses the extra-data mechanism and its apply_extra logic creates a deeply nested directory tree, permission canonicalization can fail (for example with EMFILE). Affected Flatpak versions can still report success without clearing setuid/setgid bits, leaving a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak. A local attacker who can install or update such content system-wide, or who can already execute code as a local user in cooperation with that content, can escalate privileges to root.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WPTasty AWP Classifieds another-wordpress-classifieds-plugin allows Stored XSS.This issue affects AWP Classifieds: from n/a through 4.4.10.

A vulnerability has been identified in Mendix OIDC Provider (Mendix 10 compatible) (All versions < V6.0.0), Mendix OIDC Provider (Mendix 11 compatible) (All versions < V6.0.0), Mendix OIDC Provider (Mendix 9 compatible) (All versions < V4.3.0). Affected versions of the module do not properly validate the integrity of JWTs submitted to the OIDC Provider Token Introspection endpoint, allowing tokens to be associated with legitimate token records based solely on their jti value.

This could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to hijack an account (session) when gaining access to an jti of an active token.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in VideoWhisper.com Video Share VOD video-share-vod allows Path Traversal.This issue affects Video Share VOD: from n/a through 3.15.1.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Nickboss WordPress File Upload wp-file-upload allows Path Traversal.This issue affects WordPress File Upload: from n/a through 5.3.1.
Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type vulnerability in theMarketer theMarketer themarketer allows Using Malicious Files.This issue affects theMarketer: from n/a through 1.5.9.

Pydantic Deep 0.2.18 before 0.4.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the bundled DeepResearch FastAPI app that exposes HTTP routes and the /ws/chat WebSocket. Remote attackers reaching the server bound to all interfaces can enumerate sessions, read event logs and workspace files, drive the research agent, and delete sessions.

POSTAL 2 before build 26810491 contains a sandbox escape vulnerability that allows malicious Steam Workshop mods to execute code by calling ConsoleCommand with a start file URI. Attackers can ship a batch file in a mod at the predictable workshop install path and launch it via ShellExecuteW, executing commands as the player on Windows.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Download of Code Without Integrity Check vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Server-side request forgery.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Script injection.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Heap-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Cache poisoning and Denial of service.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Remote execution.

DoS vulnerability in BS2500/BS500 Virtage Firmware.

This issue affects BladeSymphony BS2500: from 02-02 through 02-76; BladeSymphony BS500: from 01-01 through 02-76.

DoS vulnerability in BS2500/BS500 Virtage Firmware.

This issue affects BladeSymphony BS2500: from 02-02 through 02-76; BladeSymphony BS500: from 01-01 through 02-76.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Remote execution.

A flaw was found in ModemManager. When parsing a Cell Broadcast Message, some 3GPP data-coding-scheme values (8-bit and reserved character sets) are not handled. The process hits a reachable assertion and aborts. An attacker who can deliver a crafted Cell Broadcast PDU over the radio network, or via a modem AT channel, can cause ModemManager to exit. Repeated aborts can exhaust systemd's default start limit and leave the service failed.
Various logic errors in view processing can cause incorrect cached results to be returned.

n8n before 1.123.96, 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in integration nodes that build API request paths from unencoded record, table, or resource ID parameters. Attackers can supply relative path segments through untrusted input such as webhook bodies to read, modify, or delete unintended resources using the node's stored credential.

n8n before 1.123.96, 2.x before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 does not verify that the user activating a workflow can access the credentials set on its trigger nodes. An authenticated member who knows another user's credential ID can activate a workflow whose trigger uses it, causing n8n to create or delete webhooks on the connected service with that credential's privileges and deliver events from attacker-chosen resources to the member's workflow.

A security vulnerability has been detected in WOW-CMS BlizzCMS up to 1.2.1. Affected is the function Home::setconfig of the file application/modules/home/controllers/Home.php of the component Home Module. The manipulation leads to improper authorization. The attack can be initiated remotely.

A flaw was found in CRI-O. An attacker with access to the kubelet or CRI-O socket can exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the checkpoint restore functionality. This allows the attacker to delete arbitrary files and directories on the host filesystem during a checkpoint restore operation. The vulnerability arises because the system processes entries from checkpoint archive metadata without validating that the files are confined to the container's root directory.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WPTasty AWP Classifieds another-wordpress-classifieds-plugin allows Stored XSS.This issue affects AWP Classifieds: from n/a through 4.4.10.

The Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'start_date' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation requires the victim — who must hold the manage_woocommerce capability (administrator or shop manager) — to both open the attacker-crafted URL and click the start_date input field on the Export Tools page, as the injected payload is delivered via an onclick handler rather than a page-load event. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
cves.product: Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce

cves.description: An improper path validation defect in AccessibilityEnhanceProvider (com.vivo.accessibilityenhance.catcher.AccessibilityEnhanceProvider) of Accessibility Enhance allows a local malicious application to read arbitrary files outside the intended cache directory without any permission via a crafted content URI, which may lead to disclosure of user photos, documents and system information

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

In Eclipse Krazo Extensions up to and including 3.0.0, AsciiDocViewEngine passes MVC model values to Asciidoctor as document attributes without encoding them. Asciidoctor substitutes attribute references after it escapes HTML special characters and before it processes inline macros. As a result, attacker-controlled model values end up in the output as raw HTML and can inject AsciiDoc inline macros. This allows cross-site scripting in applications that render untrusted data through AsciiDoc views.

A vulnerability was found in eosphoros-ai DB-GPT up to 0.8.2. Impacted is the function _react_agent_stream_impl of the file packages/dbgpt-app/src/dbgpt_app/openapi/api_v1/agentic_data_api.py of the component Agentic Data API React Agent. The manipulation of the argument database_name results in authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 0.8.3 is recommended to address this issue. The patch is identified as 61a0460e363552e2e9722905605c86622a216d40. The affected component should be upgraded.

A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-portal. When a sandboxed application invokes Spawn() and maps two different file descriptors to the same handle, dup2() can fail. Affected Flatpak versions do not handle that failure, so a file descriptor that was open inside flatpak-portal (commonly the unfiltered D-Bus session bus) can be passed into the subsandbox. A malicious or compromised Flatpak app with no special privileges can use this to escape the sandbox.

Flask-AppBuilder before 5.3.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in ImageManager.save_file that allows authenticated users to write image files outside IMG_UPLOAD_FOLDER via unsanitized multipart filenames. Attackers with add or edit permission on a ModelView with an ImageColumn can upload filenames containing ../ segments to create or overwrite image files like static assets.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The ASCII-armor reader does not limit the length of a line. Parsing an armored message with a very long line can exhaust memory in the process. Memory use follows the input size, with a small constant factor, and is not a classic amplification.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of privileges and Remote execution.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload must be encoded as C-style escape sequences (e.g. \x3c/\x3e) at storage time so that wp_kses_post — applied on save for users lacking unfiltered_html — passes it through without stripping angle brackets; WordPress core's shortcode_parse_atts() then decodes the escapes into real HTML characters at render time.
cves.product: All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos

cves.description: The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'embedcode' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin grants the Subscriber role the edit_aiovg_videos and edit_published_aiovg_videos capabilities on activation, and save_meta_data() accepts the 'embedcode' type without checking current_user_can('unfiltered_html'), meaning any Subscriber can store a malicious shortcode containing a data: URI in the hls attribute that hls.js later processes and Plyr writes into the DOM via innerHTML.
cves.product: All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos

cves.description: A vulnerability was detected in bayang jelu up to 0.88.2. Affected by this vulnerability is the function addResourceHandlers of the file src/main/kotlin/io/github/bayang/jelu/config/WebMvcConfig.kt of the component CSV Export File Handler. The manipulation results in missing authorization. The attack can be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 0.88.3 addresses this issue. The patch is identified as a4c72815bce084865874ef2d720c01c60b6d0c6c. You should upgrade the affected component.

The Simple Calendar – Google Calendar, Events, & ICS Feeds plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '_ics_feed_file (DESCRIPTION property inside the uploaded .ics)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the victim to click the attacker-controlled link rendered in the event description, as the javascript: href payload does not fire on page load alone.
cves.product: Simple Calendar – Google Calendar, Events, & ICS Feeds

cves.description: The Easy Google Maps by Supsystic – Custom Markers, Clustering & Map Themes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file (tmp_name / name / type)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin globally widens the site's upload MIME allowlist to permit SVG files via an upload_mimes filter, meaning the attack surface exists for all uploads site-wide regardless of theme or other plugins.
cves.product: Easy Google Maps by Supsystic – Custom Markers, Clustering & Map Themes

cves.description: The Extensions for Leaflet Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'extraclasses (also icon, iconcolor, number)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The existing sanitization is ineffective for this context: wp_kses_post preserves bare double quotes (no HTML tags are required in the payload), and wp_json_encode correctly escapes the value for the JavaScript string-literal layer but the reconstituted double quote remains live when Leaflet.ExtraMarkers builds its inner HTML, allowing a single-quoted shortcode attribute value to close the HTML attribute and inject attacker-controlled event handlers.

The Extensions for Leaflet Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'overview-latlng' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by Author-level users because WordPress does not apply kses filtering to post custom fields on save, allowing raw HTML payloads such as event-handler attributes to be stored verbatim and later reflected through the unescaped debug output path.

The access rules of JTL-Shop (export/.htaccess and export/backup/.htaccess) release files with the extensions gz and zip for the export directory without withdrawing this release in the subdirectory export/backup, in which the shop stores database dumps and file backups. As a result, backup files in this directory can be downloaded without authentication by anyone who knows or guesses the file name. Up to version 5.5.5 the names of database backups consist only of a timestamp; from version 5.6.0 they contain a random component, which does not replace access control. The backups contain the complete shop database (customer data, orders, password hashes) and, for file backups, files of the shop. The access rules are only evaluated by Apache. On installations where another web server, for example nginx, delivers static files such as gz and zip directly (including nginx in front of Apache), the files remain accessible even with the corrected rules, unless the directory is blocked at server level.

FFmpeg 3.0 before 8.1.3 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_boxblur.c because query_formats() accepts pixel formats deeper than 16 bits while the blur temporary buffers hold only 2 bytes per pixel. Attackers can supply crafted 32-bit float media, such as PFM or OpenEXR images, that when processed by the boxblur filter overflow the temporary buffers, crashing applications or possibly executing code.

Sparkle 2.2.0 before 2.9.6 contains a link following vulnerability in -submitInstallerAtPath: in SUInstallerLauncher.m that builds a root updater's launcher cache path inside the console user's home directory and then deletes and creates items there without rejecting symbolic links. A local console user can pre-create that path as a symlink while a CLI tool or daemon updates a bundle as root, making root delete old files in a directory of the attacker's choosing and create a directory there that is chowned to the attacker, leading to privilege escalation.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information exposure.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

Leo through 6.8.10 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by embedding pickled data in unknown XML attributes of .leo outlines. Attackers can place a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a <t> or <v> element attribute that resolveUa passes to pickle.loads, executing code with user privileges when the outline is opened.

HCIPy through 0.7.1 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .pkl files to read_field, read_grid or read_mode_basis. Because hcipy/util/io.py selects pickle by file extension and calls pickle.load, a __reduce__ gadget in a pupil, apodizer, PSF or mode-basis file runs code with the user's privileges.

Detoxify 0.5.3 through 0.5.4 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_checkpoint that allows attackers to execute code by supplying a crafted checkpoint file. Attackers can embed a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a .ckpt file loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False to run code with the user's privileges.

JSONSchema2PoPo2 through 3.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject Python code by supplying JSON Schema default or format values that are written unescaped. Attackers can place a single quote in a string property default to break out of the literal in the generated __init__ signature, executing injected code when the generated module is imported.

A flaw was found in GIMP. The Levels configuration setter does not validate the channel enum before using it to index fixed-size per-channel arrays. A crafted XCF file with a non-destructive Levels filter can set an out-of-range channel (LUMINANCE or RGB), causing a heap out-of-bounds read and write when the file is opened. This may lead to a crash or arbitrary code execution.

HyperSpy from 1.2.0 before 2.6.0 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by embedding malicious expression strings evaluated with sympy.sympify(). Attackers can craft .hspy or .zspy files with malicious axis, Expression component, or twin function expressions that execute when victims call hs.load() or restore models.

HyperSpy from 1.4.0 before 2.6.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code by supplying crafted stored-model data in .hspy or .zspy files. Attackers can embed a malicious pickle payload in a component's _class_dump or a 'fn'-flagged _whitelist entry, which cloudpickle.loads() (dill in 1.x) runs when the victim restores the model.

Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in ReadBackupTextLen() that allows attackers to overwrite stack memory via crafted backup files. Attackers can supply overlong quoted text values decoded into a 10,000-byte stack array during convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile calls, causing crashes or potential code execution.

Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in LoadBackup() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by supplying an overlong MD5 value in a crafted backup file. Attackers can overwrite adjacent phonebook and calendar entry pointers via strcpy() into MD5Original when files are loaded with convertbackup or restore, causing crashes or potential code execution.

Gammu before 1.45.2 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in ReadWAPSettingsEntry() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted backup files with excess WAP or MMS settings entries. Attackers can supply a backup with more than four TitleNN keys in a [WAPSettings] or [MMSSettings] section, loaded via convertbackup, restore, or GSM_ReadBackupFile, causing crashes or potential code execution.

FOG Project before 1.6.0.119 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain host tokens from status/hostgetkey.php by supplying a host MAC address. Attackers can present the token to service/hostinfo.php to retrieve decrypted Active Directory join credentials and Windows product keys during deployment windows.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Authentication vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of privileges.

Dreamweaver Desktop is affected by a Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation depends on conditions beyond the attacker's control and requires user interaction in that a victim must open a malicious file. Scope is changed.

The LiteSpeed Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.9.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires comments to be open, a comment author name containing a literal quotation mark stored via WordPress's ENT_NOQUOTES save pipeline, a raw HTTP client capable of sending unencoded " and > characters in the request path, and — under default WordPress moderation — prior moderator approval of the crafted comment.

The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'design' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. The vulnerable endpoint is reached via the ?subscribe-preview=true query parameter, which is processed on template_redirect with no capability or nonce check, making it accessible to unauthenticated users.
cves.product: Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress

cves.description: A catalog zone update introducing a new zone which already exists, but in a different backend than the one storing the catalog zone, will cause a duplicate zone to be created in that backend, and (depending on the backend load order) may completely hide the existing zone.
Incorrect sanitization of received data during zone AXFR to Bind backend can cause wrong or invalid data to be serialized.
Incomplete GSS negotiation, as well as TKEY context deletion while a pending operation will need to be signed with that key, can lead to a crash.

Lookyloo is a web-based malware analysis and sandboxing platform. The pull-from-remote-instance feature allows a user to request a previously captured sample from another Lookyloo instance by specifying the target instance's URL and a capture UUID. Prior to the fix, the only restriction on the target URL was a check that the hostname, if it was a literal IP address, was not in a private range. Hostnames that resolved to private or internal addresses were not blocked, and no authentication or allowlist was enforced for anonymous users. This allowed any unauthenticated user to direct the Lookyloo server to issue HTTP requests (HEAD to the root path and GET to /json/<uuid>/status, followed by a capture download) to arbitrary internal or external hosts, effectively enabling a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack. An attacker could use this to probe internal network topology, access captures stored on internal Lookyloo instances, or leverage the server as a proxy to reach otherwise unreachable services. The vulnerability is in the website/web/__init__.py module, specifically the __get_remote_capture function and the associated pull endpoint. The security impact is unauthorized disclosure of capture data and internal service information from Lookyloo instances that are not intended to be publicly accessible.

A path traversal (ZIP slip) vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files.

In src/webextension/ephy-web-extension-manager.c, the decompress_xpi_thread() function extracts XPI archives (ZIP format) to disk using libarchive. For each archive entry, the output path is built by concatenating the intended extraction directory with the raw pathname from the archive:

 full_path = g_build_filename(path, archive_entry_pathname(entry), NULL);
 archive_entry_set_pathname(entry, full_path);
 ret = archive_write_header(ext, entry);

The libarchive extraction options did not include ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT or ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS. As a result, archive entries containing parent-directory traversal sequences (for example "../../../../../.bashrc") are written outside the intended web_extensions extraction directory.

A malicious .xpi file can therefore overwrite arbitrary files writable by the user running Epiphany, such as ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/autostart/*.desktop, or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. This can lead to persistent code execution on subsequent shell startup or GNOME login.

Exploitation requires the victim to install or open a crafted .xpi file. The reporter notes that opening an XPI can trigger extraction even when the WebExtensions feature is not enabled by default.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.rc.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2143, which adds ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT and ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS to archive_write_disk_set_options().
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2922

A **Type Confusion** has been found in the dns_to_dnsp_convert() function in dnsdata.c of the DNS server RPC module in the **Samba** package. The function copies an HINFO record from the management request into the stored DNS record without converting the request name into the two strings the stored record uses. A low-privileged network attacker or user in the DnsAdmins group adds an HINFO record through the DNS management interface. The directory process that handles the add also serves the directory's other remote calls. That process exits, which disconnects the clients that were using it, and the directory service starts a replacement process. Another add of the same kind crashes the process that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that process is replaced, so repeating the add keeps the directory remote-call service from staying available.

dns_resolve_cancel_with_name() in subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c looks up the pending query to cancel by DNS id plus a hash of the name the caller originally asked for. When a reply contains only a CNAME, the resolver sends a new query for the alias and overwrites the slot's query_hash with the hash of the alias name. After one or more CNAME hops, cancelling by the original name silently fails with -ENOENT and the query stays pending.

zsock_getaddrinfo() (exec_query() in subsys/net/lib/sockets/getaddrinfo.c) passes a pointer to its stack-local ai_state as the resolver callback context. When its semaphore wait times out, it calls dns_cancel_addr_info_with_name(), ignores the result, and returns. The CNAME re-query restarts the resolver timer, so a CNAME-only response that arrives more than about 100 ms after the query lets the getaddrinfo() wait expire first. The cancel then fails and getaddrinfo() returns. An attacker who can supply DNS responses can trigger this reliably: a malicious or compromised DNS server, an on-path attacker, or any host on the link for mDNS/LLMNR lookups. The device only has to resolve a name with getaddrinfo().

When the orphaned query later times out, dns_resolve_cb() writes the status and calls k_sem_give() on the dead stack frame. If the attacker answers the alias query instead, the callback copies attacker-supplied address data through a stale ai_arr pointer read from the reused stack. The result is a kernel fault (denial of service) or memory corruption in the calling thread's stack and whatever memory the stale pointer references.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Mamunur Rashid Classified Listing classified-listing allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Classified Listing: from n/a through 6.3.0.

Budibase server before 3.48.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the public API view row search endpoint that skips per-view permission checks due to a tableId/viewId parameter mismatch. Authenticated users with READ_ONLY role and an API key can query restricted views to read data limited to higher-privileged roles.

n8n before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the AWS Bedrock Chat Model and Embeddings AWS Bedrock nodes, where requests to a custom Bedrock runtime endpoint set in an AWS credential bypass n8n's SSRF protection. An authenticated user who can create AWS credentials can point the endpoint at internal or blocked addresses, causing n8n to send requests there and exposing the start of responses in node errors.

Wazuh-MCP-Server before commit 2bbfe12 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the blueteam_check_webshell tool because WebshellCheckInput.validate_url accepts DNS hostnames without resolving them. Attackers can supply URLs whose hostnames resolve or redirect to loopback, private, or link-local addresses, making curl reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints and leak response details.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition') vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration. When a user with editor or administrator privileges associates a HedgeDoc URL with a case, the application later issues a server-side HTTP GET request to that URL to retrieve note content. Before the fix, the stored URL was used directly without validation of its scheme, host, port, path, or userinfo, and the HTTP client followed redirects by default with no connect or read timeouts.

An authenticated attacker could therefore cause the Flowintel server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints (for example, cloud instance-metadata services, internal management interfaces, or other intranet hosts) and receive the response body, or follow a redirect chain to an unintended destination. The absence of timeouts also permitted resource-exhaustion against the server's outbound connection pool.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated account with editor or administrator role on the target case.
- The HedgeDoc integration feature is enabled (no explicit configuration gate existed before the fix).

Impact:
- Disclosure of sensitive data served by internal or cloud-metadata endpoints.
- Potential denial of service through unbounded outbound requests.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery protection bypass because getSSRFProtectionOptions passes its safe resolver as dnsLookup instead of lookup. Attackers controlling datasource hostnames can use DNS rebinding in REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth requests to reach blocked private addresses.

Heym before 0.0.154 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the workflow execute endpoint: anonymous workflows run as any signed-in caller, without an access check, using that caller's credentials and global variables. Authenticated attackers can lure signed-in users to a GET execute link for an attacker-owned anonymous workflow, which the SameSite=Lax session cookie authenticates. The attacker then reads the victim's decrypted credentials from the workflow's run history.

PDFio before 1.6.5 contains an integer underflow in _pdfioCryptoAESDecrypt() in pdfio-aes.c, which strips PKCS#7 padding before any AES block has been decrypted when an AES-encrypted string or binary value holds only its 16-byte IV. Attackers can supply a crafted AES-encrypted PDF that, when opened with pdfioFileOpen(), makes the decrypted length underflow so that _pdfioValueDecrypt() reads and writes out of bounds, crashing the application or corrupting heap memory.

Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.19 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in compose_part_body() in program/actions/mail/compose.php, which converts a text/enriched message part to HTML for the HTML editor without sanitizing the result. Attackers can send a crafted email with a text/enriched part so that script injected into the HTML editor runs in the victim's session when the victim replies to, forwards, or edits the message.

The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'price_disabled_msg' setting in versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 The uni_cpo_save_settings_data() AJAX handler applies html_entity_decode() to the output of uni_cpo_sanitize_text(), which itself already runs html_entity_decode() before wp_kses(); this double decode allows a double-entity-encoded tag to pass wp_kses as inert text and then be re-materialised as live HTML before being stored in the _cpo_price_disabled_msg post meta and later echoed via do_shortcode() on the single-product page without further escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Shop Manager-level access (edit_products) and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected product page.

The account state is checked at sign-in, but not on later requests made with a session that already exists. A user who is deactivated while signed in can keep using that session for as long as the client keeps it alive.

This could allow an authenticated remote attacker to read and change data within previous permissions for a persistent session.

Attackers who control the width of video encoded to XWD by an application that supplies tightly packed frames can make the encoder read past the frame buffer, crashing the application or leaking heap contents into the output image.

Attackers can submit @startdot diagrams with image or shapefile attributes to render local image files into PNG output and probe whether arbitrary local paths exist.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the n8n, nocodb, baserow, couchdb, elasticsearch, influxdb, and databricks datasource plugins, which skip the validateUrlForSSRF check. Authenticated builders, or unauthenticated visitors of public apps with templated URLs, can supply internal URLs or hosts to read cloud metadata credentials and internal service responses.

WhoDB from 0.88.0 before 0.132.0 contains an access control bypass in the MCP whodb_query tool, letting callers run file-writing statements without approval because the sqlguard keyword classifier omits INTO, OUTFILE and DUMPFILE. MCP clients or prompt-injected models can execute PostgreSQL lo_export or MySQL SELECT INTO OUTFILE to create files on the database host and create tables, bypassing confirmation and read-only modes.

ntfy before v2.38.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to bypass the web push endpoint allow-list by crafting a URL containing '#' or '?' characters that satisfy the [^/]+ regex pattern used to validate mozaws.net and notify.windows.com hosts. Attackers can submit an endpoint .example#.mozaws.net/push, which passes validation while Go parses the actual host as attacker.example, causing the server to send subsequent web push POST requests to an attacker-controlled or internal host.

Kestra 1.3.24 before 2.0.0 contains a timing side-channel vulnerability in BasicAuthService.isAuthenticated() that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate the administrator username. Attackers can send Basic-auth requests with candidate usernames to protected API endpoints and detect slower bcrypt checks to identify the valid account for password guessing.

picomatch through 4.0.7 contains a glob filter bypass vulnerability because globstar (**) patterns are compiled without the dotAll flag and fail to match line terminators. Attackers who control file, object key or archive entry names containing newline characters can evade ** deny patterns, causing excluded resources to be included and exposed.

A code injection vulnerability exists in Epiphany when the user invokes form autofill from the context menu on a page containing a malicious HTML form.

In embed/web-process-extension/resources/js/ephy_autofill.js, getSelector() builds a CSS selector by directly interpolating an element's id attribute:

 path.unshift(`#${el.id}`);

When the user selects an autofill entry, the browser process in embed/ephy-web-view.c previously constructed JavaScript using sprintf with the selector embedded in single quotes:

 EphyAutofill.fill(PAGE_ID, 'SELECTOR', FILL_CHOICE);

Because SELECTOR comes from attacker-controlled page content and is not escaped, a crafted id such as a'); PAYLOAD; var _=(' breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JavaScript when the script is evaluated.

The injected code runs in Epiphany's private autofill script world, which hosts EphyAutofill credential APIs and password manager save/request handlers. The reporter demonstrated a proof of concept that injects credentials into another domain and uses Ephy.permissionsManager to enumerate domains with special permissions. Full exfiltration of all saved passwords was not demonstrated but may be possible given the privileges of this context.

Exploitation requires the victim to visit a malicious page, right-click on a form field, and choose an Autofill context menu item. This is a deliberate user action but does not require installing software or entering credentials manually.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.beta.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2147, which replaces sprintf-based script evaluation with a WebKit user message and jsc_value_object_invoke_method() passing the selector as a typed string argument.
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2921

ClassroomIO through 1.0.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated course members to access other tenants' newsfeed posts by supplying a foreign feedId under their own courseId. Attackers can read, react to, and comment on cross-organization posts, while team members or org admins can also overwrite content, pin flags, and delete them.

Otter – Page Builder Blocks & Extensions for Gutenberg before 3.2.12 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows Contributor-level attackers to make the server contact arbitrary hosts via crafted Mailchimp API keys. Attackers can POST to the otter/v1/form/editor REST route with an apiKey whose data-center segment embeds a host, following redirects to internal services and reading partial responses.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The default ASCII-armor parser accepts Unicode dash characters in armor framing and ignores leading quote characters. A crafted byte stream can be parsed as one message by this tolerant parser and as a different message by a strict ASCII-armor parser. The strict mode is opt-in; the default parser remains tolerant.

An attacker might be able to forge its own source IP, smuggle DNS records or bypass EDNS options filtering via a specially crafted DNS query when EDNS Client Subnet is enabled between DNSdist and its backend.
A catalog zone provider can add a root zone as member and cause PowerDNS to provision it from the given source.

libexpat 2.6.0 through 2.11.0 built with XML_GE=0 and XML_UNICODE contains an out-of-bounds read in storeSelfEntityValue() because narrow string literals are treated as wide strings. Attackers can supply an XML document whose DOCTYPE declares a general entity to expose adjacent static memory through the entity value or crash the parser.

The Dilemma Lite WordPress plugin through 1.1.1 does not sanitise or escape the choices of dilemmas submitted by visitors before outputting them in the admin dashboard and on the front end, allowing unauthenticated attackers to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators.

FFmpeg 7.1 before 9.1 contains a memory leak vulnerability in eb_receive_packet() in libavcodec/libsvtav1.c that returns without unreferencing the queued input frame when eb_send_frame() fails. Attackers can supply crafted video in which some frames lack Dolby Vision metadata to an SVT-AV1 encode with Dolby Vision RPU coding enabled, leaking each rejected frame's buffers or aborting in av_frame_move_ref() in builds with assertions enabled.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xsub_encode() in libavcodec/xsubenc.c that only warns when a subtitle has no rectangles and then dereferences rects[0]. Attackers can supply crafted PGS or DVB subtitles that decode to empty subtitle events, crashing applications that pass decoded subtitles directly to the XSUB encoder.

Pillow through 13.1.0 contains an integer overflow in the ImageMath integer divide and modulo operators (DIV_I and MOD_I in src/_imagingmath.c), which guard only against a zero divisor, so dividing INT32_MIN by -1 raises a hardware divide exception. Attackers can supply a crafted TIFF that decodes to a mode I image containing INT32_MIN, crashing applications that run an ImageMath divide or modulo with a -1 operand on it.

GNU m4 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in reload_frozen_state() in src/freeze.c. When processing a malicious frozen-state file via the -R option, an attacker can trigger an oversized allocation request that crashes the program, causing denial of service.


This issue was fixed in commit 69aef802fb25ab600d37210f44e5128633cbc432.
A race condition in the handling of the forward notification requests queue can lead to a crash if too many UDP notify packets for a given zone are received in a short time frame.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Filesystem access for attacker.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. Display and Debug formatting of User IDs and notation data does not escape control characters. When an application prints those values, a crafted User ID or notation can misrender the identity or alter terminal output.

An attacker allowed to send AXFR or IXFR queries can cause an outgoing TCP connection to the backend to be stuck, causing a denial of service to other clients trying to reuse the same outgoing connection.
An attacker can cause a denial of service by sending crafted HTTP queries to the internal webserver. The webserver is not enabled by default and is protected by an ACL.

An attacker can trigger a large memory use by cancelling QUIC streams while DNSdist is retrieving the response from its backend. Instead of releasing the memory corresponding to the cancelled stream right away, DNSdist was mistakenly keeping it around until the end of the QUIC connection.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the TEST_CONNECTION ability to reach arbitrary hosts by supplying body-controlled datasource options. Attackers can set kind, plugin_id, and host options for plugins like influxdb or elasticsearch to reach loopback, internal services, or cloud metadata endpoints exposing IAM credentials.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an arbitrary file read and SSRF vulnerability in the SMTP plugin that allows authenticated app builders to pass object values to Nodemailer. Attackers can set textContent or htmlContent to path or href content objects to email server files or internal cloud metadata responses to themselves.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to make the server fetch internal URLs via the gRPC v2 proto_file_url option. Attackers can target loopback, private, cloud metadata, or redirect-controlled addresses, or serve oversized responses that are buffered and parsed synchronously, causing denial of service.

When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and a caching HTTP reverse proxy is used in front of DNSdist, it is possible to pollute the cache of the HTTP reverse proxy by sending DNS over HTTPS GET queries with a body. The MCUmgr SMP client matched an incoming response to a pending command in smp_client_response_discover() (subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/smp_client/src/client.c) using only the 8-bit sequence number and the operation. It did not check the transport the response arrived on, or the group and command ID. smp_process_request_packet() hands every MGMT_OP_READ_RSP/MGMT_OP_WRITE_RSP packet received on any SMP transport to smp_client_single_response(), so a response from any SMP peer could complete any pending client command.

On a device that is both an SMP server (for example over Bluetooth LE or UDP) and an SMP client (CONFIG_SMP_CLIENT, for example using img_mgmt_client to update a companion MCU over UART), a peer on the server transport can send up to 256 forged response packets while a client operation is pending and have one of them accepted as the reply from the managed device. Non-matching responses are dropped silently. The response path bypasses the server command handlers, so restricting which server groups a peer may use does not prevent it.

The attacker can forge the results of client operations. For example, a forged image-upload offset makes img_mgmt_client_upload() report success after only part of the image was sent, a forged image-state response can report arbitrary versions or flags, and any pending command can be forced to fail. No memory corruption results: the response callbacks bound-check the decoded data. The target's own image validation limits the result to failed or suppressed updates and disrupted management operations. The fix restricts matching to commands sent on the same transport with the same group and command ID. Responses from a different peer on the same transport are still not distinguished.

The system call verifier z_vrfy_k_thread_stack_space_get() in kernel/thread.c checked the result of K_SYSCALL_OBJ(thread, K_OBJ_THREAD) with the CHECKIF() macro instead of K_OOPS(). CHECKIF() compiles to if (0) when CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS is selected, and becomes an assertion when CONFIG_ASSERT_ON_ERRORS is selected. In both cases, the kernel-object validation result for the user-supplied thread pointer is ignored, or is a no-op when assertions are disabled.

On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE, CONFIG_INIT_STACKS and CONFIG_THREAD_STACK_INFO plus one of those check modes, a user-mode thread can call k_thread_stack_space_get() with an arbitrary pointer. That pointer can be a fake struct k_thread in its own memory, or a thread object it has no permission on. z_impl_k_thread_stack_space_get() then dereferences thread->stack_info in supervisor mode and scans memory starting at the attacker-chosen stack_info.start.

The syscall returns the number of leading 0xAA bytes at that address. This gives an unprivileged thread a limited oracle on arbitrary kernel or peripheral memory, and allows privileged reads of attacker-selected addresses, including MMIO. No write primitive results. The default CONFIG_RUNTIME_ERROR_CHECKS configuration is not affected. The fix replaces the CHECKIF() with K_OOPS() so the object check is always enforced.
